plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: In the wild, poinsettia is a tall, open shrub or small tree that can reach 3–4 metres. In December it is topped with fiery crowns of bright bracts that glow against the dark green leaves. The tiny yellow true flowers cluster at the centre of each crown.
plants.bloomingSeason: December, in the short days of the Northern Hemisphere winter
plants.location: Native to Mexico and Central America, where wild plants bloom in December. It is also widely grown in tropical gardens.
plants.funFact: The showy red 'petals' are modified leaves called bracts. The real flowers are the small yellow buttons at their centre.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This graceful evergreen shrub opens silky, often lightly scented blooms when most other plants have gone dormant. Its glossy dark leaves set off single or semi-double flowers with golden stamens. Bees and other pollinators visit them on mild winter days.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn into early winter, usually October or November through December or January
plants.location: Native to Japan. It is widely grown in the mild-winter gardens of the southern United States, Europe and Australia.
plants.funFact: Sasanqua camellias flower earlier than the more familiar Camellia japonica, so they open the camellia season each year.
